declarations.name: Causal.IsSpacetimeExtension.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] {N : Type v} [TopologicalSpace N] [Nonempty N] {CN : Causality N} {C : Causality M} {ι : N → M} [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] (hι : IsSpacetimeExtension CN C ι), CN.CausallyArcConnected → CN.FutureOneConnected → CN.IsCausal → (∀ (I : Set ℝ) (δ : ℝ → N), CN.FutureInextensible ⊤ I δ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, CN.ChronalCurveOn ⊤ δ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, CN.Iminus ⊤ {δ t} = Set.univ) → (∀ (x : N), ∃ S, CN.IsCauchySurface S ∧ S ⊆ CN.Iplus ⊤ {x}) → ∀ (Ũ : Opens M) (p : M), ¬ C.FutureBoundaryChart hι.rangeOpens Ũ p
declarations.what: Part (a), the deliverable. It is the time reversal of the past corollary IsSpacetimeExtension.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType, with the same binder order: hι, hcac, hfoc, hcaus, hA, hB, Ũ, p. The hypotheses on N are the same ladder nodes, with (A⁻) in the shape of the open-set time reversal Causality.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType at W = ⊤, and `= univ` as in the past corollary. (B⁻) reads S ⊆ I⁺(x).
declarations.proof: hι.dual.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType, the past corollary for the extension IsSpacetimeExtension.dual : IsSpacetimeExtension CN.dual C.dual ι. Its arguments are dual_causallyArcConnectedOn.2 hcac, dual_futureOneConnected.2 hfoc and dual_isCausal.2 hcaus. (A⁻) becomes (A) for CN.dual by reversing the curve, through dual_pastInextensible_iff and CurveOn.neg, which is the conversion of Causality.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType at W = ⊤. (B⁻) becomes (B) for CN.dual through dual_isCauchySurfaceOn, with CN.dual.Iminus = CN.Iplus by rfl. The conclusion ¬ C.dual.PastBoundaryChart hι.dual.rangeOpens Ũ p is the goal with no rewrite. FutureBoundaryChart is C.dual.PastBoundaryChart by definition, and hι.dual.rangeOpens = hι.rangeOpens holds by rfl: both are ⟨range ι, _⟩, and the dual's isOpenEmbedding field is hι.isOpenEmbedding. Probe.lean checks both rfl facts as `example`s.

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart
declarations.statement: ∀ (W Ũ : Opens ℝ) (p : ℝ), ¬ timelikeLine.FutureBoundaryChart W Ũ p
declarations.what: The time reversal of timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart: no open set of the timelike line has a future boundary chart at any point. It is not in the dispatch. I added it because without it item 5 would claim, for the new witness, something no Lean declaration proves: that the witness shows the hypotheses consistent and not the predicate inhabited.
declarations.proof: The one-dimensional argument with the order reversed. Field (vi) is taken at K = [γ̃ 1, p]. If σ 0 ≥ γ̃ 1, the intermediate value theorem (intermediate_value_Icc', since σ decreases from σ 0 to σ 1 < γ̃ 1) puts γ̃ 1 on σ: at t = 0 that gives σ 0 ∈ V ⊆ W, and at t > 0 it gives σ t ∈ K. If σ 0 < γ̃ 1, then γ̃ 1 ≫ σ 0 in Ũ for the reversed line, and field (iii) puts σ 0 in V ⊆ W. The relations of timelikeLine.dual are read with `change` (see kb_proposals).

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ
declarations.statement: ∀ (I : Set ℝ) (δ : ℝ → ℝ), timelikeLine.FutureInextensible ⊤ I δ → ⋃ t ∈ I, timelikeLine.Iminus ⊤ {δ t} = Set.univ
declarations.what: (A⁻) on the timelike line, the time reversal of timelikeLine_iUnion_Iplus_eq_univ.
declarations.proof: For x, take t₁ ∈ I. If x < δ t₁, then x ∈ I⁻(δ t₁). Otherwise δ t₁ ∈ J⁻({x + 1}), and FutureInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jminus_of_isCausal makes δ meet the Cauchy surface {x + 1} (timelikeLine_isCauchySurface_singleton), which lies above x.

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_exists_cauchy_Iplus
declarations.statement: ∀ (x : ℝ), ∃ S, timelikeLine.IsCauchySurface S ∧ S ⊆ timelikeLine.Iplus ⊤ {x}
declarations.what: (B⁻) on the timelike line, the time reversal of timelikeLine_exists_cauchy_Iminus. The surface is {x + 1}.

declarations.name: Causal.timelikeLine_exp_not_futureBoundaryChart
declarations.statement: ∀ (Ũ : Opens ℝ) (p : ℝ), ¬ timelikeLine.FutureBoundaryChart exp_isSpacetimeExtension.rangeOpens Ũ p
declarations.what: Part (a)'s kb/0011 witness. Every hypothesis of IsSpacetimeExtension.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType holds for exp : ℝ → ℝ, the extension of the timelike line into itself onto (0, ∞). findings: No paper label is involved: 2312.07443 is not ledgered, and the time-reversed statements are not in the paper. These findings concern the programme.

The time reversal costs no new transport lemma. IsSpacetimeExtension.dual reverses both causalities along the same ι, and the past corollary for it is the future one for ι, up to two rfl facts: C.FutureBoundaryChart W Ũ p = C.dual.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p, and hι.dual.rangeOpens = hι.rangeOpens. Probe.lean checks both as `example`s. The planner's question, whether the second is rfl or needs a rewrite, is answered: it is rfl, and the theorem's conclusion is stated at hι.rangeOpens with no cast.

No Lean declaration inhabits FutureBoundaryChart. The past chart has the layer-3 instance Causal.minkowski_pastBoundaryChart (the half-space {t > 0} of 𝐌^{1+n}, n ≥ 1, at 0). No future chart exists in Lean, and the new timelikeLine_not_futureBoundaryChart shows the timelike line has none. So the time-reversed theorems (the open-set not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType, the A- and B-closed-ambient forms and the two new ones) have witnesses of consistency, not of non-vacuity. The natural instance is {t < 0} of 𝐌^{1+n} at 0, through the isometry t ↦ −t, or Minkowski space's dual causality. That is layer 3 and is left to the planner; I did not attempt it, since layer 1 imports no model.

Part (b)'s witness on (0, ∞) is exactly as the planner described. (B⁻) on ℝ is carried by the dual extension exp_isSpacetimeExtension.dual, through the existing past transport exists_isCauchySurfaceOn_subset_Iminus. No future transport lemma was needed.

(A)'s time reversal in the closed ambient (not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA_of_isClosed_le and its GH form) still has no timelike-line witness. With timelikeLine_iUnion_Iminus_eq_univ now in FlrwType, one would also need (A⁻) on (0, ∞): (A) for timelikeLine.dual carried by exp_isSpacetimeExtension.dual.iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_pastInextensible, then converted back from C.dual to C. That is the converse of dual_iUnion_Iplus_eq_of_futureInextensible. It is outside this dispatch and is recorded here for the planner.
questions: (A⁻) and (B⁻) for the extension are read as the exact time reversals of the past corollary's (A) and (B) at W = ⊤. (A⁻): every CN.FutureInextensible ⊤ I δ, chronal on its segments, has ⋃ t ∈ I, CN.Iminus ⊤ {δ t} = univ, with `univ` as in the past corollary and not `⊤`. (B⁻): every x has a Cauchy surface S of N with S ⊆ CN.Iplus ⊤ {x}. This is the dispatch's wording. It is the open-set time reversal's shape at W = ⊤, and is no new reading of Sbierski's Prop 3.6.
